title: Dario Amodei calls out rival AI CEOs over their AI messaging
excerpt: The Anthropic CEO said that suggestions that he supports handing over political governance to AI is "absurd."
content_html:
Dario Amodei accuses rival AI CEOs of ‘vibes-based commercial and political positioning’

By Katherine Li

You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

2026-11-25T23:56:50.957Z

Dario Amodei said Wednesday that humans should keep control of political decisions, even as AI takes on more complex tasks, from driving cars to writing software.

In a lengthy post on X on Wednesday, the Anthropic CEO said that rival AI executives are paying lip service to human control over AI while continuing to release products that increasingly automate human tasks.

“What is happening is that there’s a sort of vibes-based commercial and political positioning that some AI CEOs are engaging in, where they repeat slogans like ‘human control and agency,’ or ‘AI should be just a tool,’ without actually doing anything different in their products or taking seriously the difficult questions that lie behind these slogans," Amodei wrote.

Amodei was responding to an Axios report that some Anthropic employees favor handing certain decisions to superintelligent AI. The report cited his past remarks and noted that rival executives had defended human control without naming Anthropic.

Among the examples Axios cited were some of Amodei's past comments in a February interview with The New York Times about how much control people should retain as AI systems become more capable.

"I would argue that in many cases, we do want to stay in charge," Amodei told NYT journalist Ross Douthat in a video interview. "That's a choice we want to make, even in some cases when we think the humans, on average, make kind of worse decisions."

Amodei said there were safety-critical cases where handing a task over to AI could make sense, but cautioned that society could only adapt so fast.

On Wednesday, Amodei called it "absurd" to suggest he wants humans to surrender their free will to AI. He separately said handing political control to AI was a "terrible idea."

“This is not AI ‘running the world,’ but AI driving a car, designing a cancer drug, or writing software end-to-end,” Amodei wrote. "Here, my view is mixed. AI doing more complete or larger tasks is economically valuable and can drive important advances in software, medicine, transportation, energy, etc. It is clearly desirable in many cases and will save a lot of lives.”

“I don't think that other AI leaders or AI companies have significantly different views from me on whether specific tasks should be automated,” Amodei said, adding that companies across the industry are rolling out increasingly sophisticated AI models.

Amodei, however, said there is a caveat to AI automation: some AI deployments might need to slow or stop if they risk serious job disruption.

"In some contexts, using AI in too end-to-end a manner may be a cause of serious job disruption," Amodei said, "And it may make sense to slow or even stop some AI deployments to give people more time to adapt."
